facts.raw_span: A 70-year-old Japanese man presented with dysphagia
cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge
Enterobacter cloacae was cultured from the wound
lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness without sensory loss
A 70-year-old Japanese man presented with dysphagia
cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge
Enterobacter cloacae was cultured from the wound
lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness without sensory loss

concepts.why: The patient was diagnosed with T3N0M0 esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
Enterobacter cloacae was cultured from the wound.
The patient developed a refractory anastomotic fistula.
The patient developed worsening low back pain, fever, and lumbar spinal tenderness.
The patient had a history of radiotherapy for laryngeal cancer.
The patient had a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
The patient developed cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge.
The patient developed worsening low back pain, fever, and lumbar spinal tenderness.

rationales.F03: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma diagnosis directly supports C01.
rationales.F06: History of radiotherapy for laryngeal cancer supports C05.
rationales.F09: Enterobacter cloacae cultured from the wound supports C02 and potentially C04 due to the later development of symptoms consistent with spondylodiscitis.
rationales.F12: Lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness without sensory loss strongly support C04, indicating a possible infection of the spinal disc.
